points.quote: The desktop entry adds `electron-browser/desktop.main.js` and `desktop.contribution.js`. It also adds native service implementations ... and other desktop-only contributions.
The web entry adds `browser/web.main.ts`, which comes with `web.factory.ts` and `web.api.ts`. It also adds web variants
`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` is the common entry. ... Both `workbench.desktop.main.ts` and `workbench.web.main.ts` start with `import './workbench.common.main.js'`.
Platform-specific implementations register against the same service interfaces, so the shared code never needs to know which one it got.
Everything reachable from the common entry is therefore in both builds. ... Leaving it out of an entry file leaves it out of that build.
A feature's code is loaded only if some entry file imports its `*.contribution.ts` file, directly or transitively.
